previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute viral gastroenteritis causing severe diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, which exacerbated her chronic pancreatitis and gastroparesis. Over nine days, her symptoms resolved with conservative management including IV fluids, low-dose narcotics, and gradual resumption of tube feeds up to 50 cc/hr. Her type 1 diabetes was stabilized with adjusted insulin dosing, and psychiatric symptoms remained controlled on her baseline regimen. Stool studies ruled out bacterial pathogens. Pain management was transitioned from IV Dilaudid to oral hydromorphone for discharge, with tramadol discontinued due to patient refusal during admission. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume her prior insulin regimen, continue tube feeds, and follow up with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ woman with h/o IDDM since age ___ c/b severe gastroparesis, 
chronic pancreatitis from pancreas divisum, chronic abdominal 
pain on narcotics, and borderline personality disorder who is 
admitted with worsening abdominal pain, diarrhea, inability to 
take POs, and hyperglycemia. 
.  
# Diarrhea, inability to tolerate POs: Similar to typical flare 
of chronic pancreatitis with secondary to pancreatic divisum.  
Patient was initially started on bowel rest with gentle IVF 
hydration.  C. diff and stool cultures was negative.  Pain was 
controlled with IV Dilaudid PRN while the patient was not 
tolerating POs per previously established guidelines for 
hospital care.  Zofran PRN was given for nausea.  PPI was 
continued.  Diet was gradually advanced as tolerated.  However, 
patient reported persistent abdominal pain and discomfort with 
PO intake and tube feeds.  Tube feeds were initiated at rate of 
5 cc/hr and gradually increased per previously discussed plan 
with intermittent success, as feeds were discontinued frequently 
secondary to pain.  Several multidisciplinary meetings were held 
to discuss further plan of care.  Pain service was consuled 
about the possibility of celiac block, which the patient 
refused.  GJ tube was revised prior to discharge.  Despite 
reported inability for any significant PO intake for over a 
month per patient, she was noted to have a net ___ lbs gain over 
that time period and a stable serum albumin.  Given that her 
nutritional status was intact, her IV pain regimen was weaned 
and transitioned to PO.  Patient was medically safe for 
discharge with stable sugars.  
.  
# Diabetes: Hyperglycemic on presentation, without evidence of 
infection.  Chest radiograph with no acute process, urine 
analysis within normal limits.  The patient was followed by 
___ service during hospitalization.  Home insulin regimen 
adjusted given NPO status.  Glargine was increased to 34 units 
qhs with increases in sliding scale.  Sugars were in the 200 
range prior to discharge.
.  
# Borderline personality disorder: Multidisciplinary meetings, 
including the PCP, were held frequently to discuss long term 
goals of care for the patient.  The patient was followed by 
psychiatry during this hospitalization.  The patient denied 
suicidal ideations or plan during this admission.  Will need 
outpatient follow up.
.  
# Constipation: Secondary to narcotic medications, patient 
developed constipation and aggressive bowel regimen was 
continued in house.  Also with bright red blood per rectum on 
several incidences secondary to known hemorrhoids.  Hematocrit 
and vital signs were stable throughout hospital course.  Will 
continue aggressive bowel regimen as an outpatient.
.
# R wrist pain s/p fall: Patient fell while walking to the bath, 
with no evidence of fracture of right wrist or shoulder.  
Evaluated by orthopedics team.  With right wrist sprain and 
questionable right shoulder rotator cuff tear.  Ortho did not 
recommend further imaging while in house.  Her wrist was placed 
in a splint and she was told to wear a sling when out of bed.  
She will have an MRI scheduled by PCP as an outpatient and 
follow up with Dr. ___ orthopedics after MRI is 
performed.
.
# Vaginal discharge: The patient reported chronic slow sanginous 
discharge from vagina over the past ___ months.  Hematoctit 
remained stable.  Patient deferred pelvic exam by primary team.  
Will need follow up as an outpatient with PCP.
.
# Asthma: She was continued on outpatient albuterol and advair.

HISTORY:  ___ female with chronic abdominal pain and a clogged
GJ-tube.

COMPARISON:  G-tube exchange on ___.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ were present.  Dr.
___, the interventional radiology attending, was present and
supervising throughout.

ANESTHESIA:  1 mg of Dilaudid and 1 mg of Versed were administered during
continuous monitoring of vital signs.

PROCEDURE:  The risks and benefits of the procedure were explained to the
patient and written informed consent was obtained.  A preprocedural timeout
was performed per ___ protocol.  The region around the patient's existing GJ
tube was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Viscous lidocaine
was instilled in the region around the existing gastrostomy tube tract for
local anesthesia.  The end of the existing gastrostomy tube was cut to permit
release of the locking pigtail.  A 0.035 stiff guidewire was advanced through
the existing gastrostomy tube.  As the existing gastrostomy tube was removed,
however, the distal end of the wire dislodged from the jejunum.  Therefore, a
6 ___ sheath was advanced over the wire with the tip of the sheath in the
stomach.  A combination of angled glide and C2 catheters were used to direct
the glide wire into the jejunum.  Once access was obtained with the wires into
the jejunum, the 6 ___ sheath was removed.  A 14 ___ ___
gastrojejunostomy catheter was placed over the wire with the tip in the
proximal jejunum.  This was confirmed by injection of a small volume of
contrast.  The pigtail of the gastrojejunostomy catheter was formed in the
duodenum.  The external portion of the catheter was secured with a StatLock
device.  Sterile dressings were applied.  The patient tolerated the procedure
well without immediate post-procedural complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful exchange of a GJ tube, the tip in the proximal
jejunum.  The tube is ready to use.
